question: A portable CMS designer proposes 'DLY' to mean DELAY. Using Section 1D.08 and Table 1D-3, is this acceptable and why?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No, this is not acceptable. "DLY" appears in Table 1D-3 as an unacceptable abbreviation because, while intended to mean "Delay," it is commonly misinterpreted by road users as "Daily." Section 1D.08 mandates that Table 1D-3 abbreviations shall not be used on any traffic control device, and this requirement applies to changeable message signs through Section 2L.05. Standards (mandatory): - "The abbreviations shown in Table 1D-3 shall not be used in connection with traffic control devices because of their potential to be misinterpreted by road users." - "Abbreviations displayed on CMS shall comply with the provisions of Section 1D.08." - If "Delay" needs to be abbreviated on a portable changeable message sign, only an abbreviation authorized by Table 1D-2 may be used: "When the word messages shown in Table 1D-2 need to be abbreviated on a portable changeable message sign, the abbreviations shown in Table 1D-2 shall be used." Guidance (recommended): - If any Table 1D-2 abbreviation with a prompt word were used instead, "the abbreviations for the words listed in Table 1D-2 that also show a prompt word should not be used on a portable changeable message sign... unless the prompt word shown in Table 1D-2 either precedes or follows the abbreviation, as applicable." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 1D-3, "Unacceptable Abbreviations," which lists DLY with intended word "Delay" and common misinterpretation "Daily," confirming the proposed abbreviation is expressly prohibited. Citations: - Section 1D.08 Standard §4 (p.34) - Section 2L.05 Standard §6 (p.516) - Section 1D.08 Standard §2 (p.34) - Section 1D.08 Guidance §3 (p.34) - Table 1D-3 (p.37)
gold_answer: No. DLY is explicitly prohibited because it can be misinterpreted as DAILY.
